newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian market recovers, BUX index ends at new high.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian market recovers, BUX index ends at new high.

text.p: One day of downward correction was enough for the Budapest Stock Exchange to gain new strength and finish at a new all-time high on Thursday despite intraday profit-takings, market participants said.
"Prices ran away after opening and there was some profit-taking during the session," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 7,444.27 points, up 71.19 points or 0.97 percent.
"(Chemicals) TVK, oil and gas company MOL and tile maker Zalakeramia were particularly affected by profit-takings," Nagy added.

Roger Monson, chief equity strategist at Daiwa Europe in London said the Hungarian market merited the current investor focus, with domestic interest rates trends and international market sentiment also favouring the bourse.
"In the context of a good, healthy equity environment Hungary deserves the attention it is getting," Monson said, adding Hungary has a recovering economy and a very good corporate performance.

"One last thing that is still coming into play is the steady small steps down, reducing interest rates as inflation comes down," he added. "That will continue to help the market along with the other factors.
But Monson said the market was not particularly cheap.
"(The market) can go further but we shouldn't be having any illusions about fantastic games from here like the doubling in price in twelve months."

Thursday's relatively low turnover contributed to the fact that the market could not hold its early gains, Nagy said, and attributed the smaller volume to the fact that many foreign investors scaled down their buys waiting to see lower prices.
Final turnover figures was not yet available but volume of traded shares and compensation coupons amounted to 1,341,687 units.
TVK leapt to a new high of 4,050 forints before retreating to close at 3,885, down 25, while MOL finished at 4,325 forints, down 15, in not particularly high turnover.
Zalakeramia finished at 8,050 forints, up 50, but below the day's peak of 8,160.
Elsewhere, OTP Bank rallied to a new high of 6,600 forints, before closing at 6,595, up 345.

One trader said earlier OTP benefited from the sale price of K&H Bank in which an around 10 percent stake would be sold to the consortium of Belgium's Kredietbank and Ireland's Irish Life Plc for $30 million, which represents 567.3 percent of the face value, the best price in Hungarian bank privatisation.
